:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y) = x^2 + 2y^2 +x$ that passes through the point where $(x,y) = (1, 1).$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y) = (1,1)$ can be found by computing $\nabla f(1,1).$  

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y) = (1,1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+x)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+x)\,j \\  & =(2x+0+1)\,i+(0+4y+0)\,j \\  & =(2x+1)\,i+4y\,j \\ ∇f(1,1) & =(2(1)+1)\,i+4(1)\,j \\  & =3\,i+4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we want a unit normal vector, we normalize $\nabla f(1,1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(1,1)}{‖∇f(1,1)‖} & =\frac{3\,i+4\,j}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3\,i+4\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-y$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(0,1).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(x,y)=(0,1)$ can be found by computing $∇f(0,1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-y)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-y)\,j \\  & =(4x+0-0)\,i+(0+4y-1)\,j \\  & =4x\,i+(4y-1)\,j \\ ∇f(0,1) & =4(0)\,i+(4(1)-1)\,j \\  & =3\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(0,1):$

$$
\frac{∇f(0,1)}{‖∇f(0,1)‖}=\frac{3\,j}{3}=j
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=2x+4y+5xy$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,1).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,1)$, can be found by computing $∇f(2,1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(2,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x+4y+5xy)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x+4y+5xy)\text{ }j \\  & =(5y+2)\text{ }i+(5x+4)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(2,1) & =(5\cdot 1+2)\text{ }i+(5\cdot 2+4)\text{ }j \\  & =7i+14j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(2,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(2,1)}{‖∇f(2,1)‖} & =\frac{7i+14j}{\sqrt{{7}^{2}+(14)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{7i+14j}{7\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}(i+2\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{x}+2\sqrt{y}$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,4).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(x,y)=(1,4)$ can be found by computing $∇f(1,4).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{x}+2\sqrt{y})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{x}+2\sqrt{y})\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\,j \\ ∇f(1,4) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1}}\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,i+\frac{1}{2}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(1,4)}{‖∇f(1,4)‖} & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}(i+j)}{‖\frac{1}{2}(i+j)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}})}\cdot \frac{1}{2}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+j).\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $g(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,1).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point  where $(x,y)=(1,1)$, can be found by computing $∇g(1,1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $g(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & ={g}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{g}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy))\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{xy}\cdot y\,i+\frac{1}{xy}\cdot x\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\,i+\frac{1}{y}\,j \\ ∇g(1,1) & =\frac{1}{(1)}\,i+\frac{1}{(1)}\,j \\  & =i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇g(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇g(1,1)}{‖∇g(1,1)‖} & =\frac{i+j}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$, can be found by computing $∇f(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\text{ }j \\  & =2x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j \\ ∇f(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) & =2(-\frac{1}{2})\text{ }i+2(\frac{1}{2})\text{ }j \\  & =-i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})}{‖∇f(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})‖} & =\frac{-i+j}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-i+j}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-j)\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=x+3y-2xy$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(\frac{3}{2},1).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(\frac{3}{2},1)$, can be found by computing $∇f(\frac{3}{2},1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(\frac{3}{2},1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+3y-2xy)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+3y-2xy)\text{ }j \\  & =(1-2y)\text{ }i+(3-2x)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(\frac{3}{2},1) & =(1-2(1))\text{ }i+(3-2(\frac{3}{2}))\text{ }j \\  & =-i\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(\frac{3}{2},1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(\frac{3}{2},1)}{‖∇f(\frac{3}{2},1)‖} & =\frac{-i}{1}=-i\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)={e}^{x+y}+x+y$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(0,0).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(0,0)$, can be found by computing $∇f(0,0).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(0,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x+y}+x+y)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x+y}+x+y)\text{ }j \\  & =({e}^{x+y}+1)\text{ }i+({e}^{x+y}+1)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(0,0) & =({e}^{0+0}+1)\text{ }i+({e}^{0+0}+1)\text{ }j \\  & =2i+2j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(0,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(0,0)}{‖∇f(0,0)‖} & =\frac{2i+2j}{\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2i+2j}{2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\frac{x+y}{x-y}$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-2,-1).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(x,y)=(-2,-1)$ can be found by computing $∇f(-2,-1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-2,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x+y}{x-y})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x+y}{x-y})\,j \\  & =\frac{1(x-y)-(x+y)(1)}{(x-y)^{2}}\,i+\frac{1(x-y)-(x+y)(-1)}{(x-y)^{2}}\,j \\  & =-\frac{2y}{(x-y)^{2}}\,i+\frac{2x}{(x-y)^{2}}\,j \\ ∇f(-2,-1) & =-\frac{2(-1)}{(-2-(-1))^{2}}\,i+\frac{2(-2)}{(-2-(-1))^{2}}\,j \\  & =2\,i-4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(-2,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(-2,-1)}{‖∇f(-2,-1)‖} & =\frac{2\,i-4\,j}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}(2\,i-4\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(i-2\,j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}(\,i-2\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,-2).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(x,y)=(2,-2)$ can be found by computing $∇f(2,-2).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(2,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}))j \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}})}{1+{(\frac{y}{x})}^{2}}\,i+\frac{(\frac{1}{x})}{1+{(\frac{y}{x})}^{2}}\,j \\  & =-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,i+\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,j \\ ∇f(2,-2) & =-\frac{(-2)}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\,i+\frac{2}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\,j \\  & =\frac{2}{8}\,i+\frac{2}{8}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(2,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(2,-2)}{‖∇f(2,-2)‖} & =\frac{\frac{1}{4}(i+j)}{‖\frac{1}{4}(i+j)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{4}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}})}\cdot \frac{1}{4}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+j).\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(5,4).$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(5,4)$, can be found by computing $∇f(5,4).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(5,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}})\text{ }j \\  & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\text{ }i-\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\text{ }j \\ ∇f(5,4) & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{(5)^{2}-(4)^{2}}}\text{ }i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{(5)^{2}-(4)^{2}}}\text{ }j \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{9}}i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{9}}j \\  & =\frac{5}{3}i-\frac{4}{3}j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(5,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(5,4)}{‖∇f(5,4)‖} & =\frac{\frac{5}{3}i-\frac{4}{3}j}{\sqrt{{(\frac{5}{3})}^{2}+{(-\frac{4}{3})}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{5}{3}i-\frac{4}{3}j}{\frac{\sqrt{41}}{3}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{41}}{41}(5i-4j)\end{aligned}
$$
